alternatives: The existing flat claim_status vocabulary extended with more values.
Stage inferred at display time from score thresholds.
claims.boundary: Governed Indus claims: extracted literature claims and anchor-reading claims, in the AEE wiring (aee_core), the claims API, and every display surface.
falsification_tests: A governed claim representation (API response, stored record, or rendered surface) that carries a score or verdict but no lifecycle stage defeats this claim.
A lifecycle stage value outside the five-value set in any governed artifact defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: claim_status already does this job and a second axis is redundant bookkeeping.
metadata.verdict_rule: Stage is an explicit stored field with its own transition log; no code path derives it from a score or from claim_status.

claims.text: Every governed Indus claim carries a lifecycle stage in the fixed set {created, checked, explained, accepted, digested}, stored and displayed separately from its AEE score, its program verdict, and its extraction status.

alternatives: Automated advancement to accepted for claims above a score threshold with human review afterwards.
claims.boundary: All stage transitions in the AEE wiring, the research loop, intake, and any batch or scheduled process.
falsification_tests: A stage-transition log entry advancing a claim past checked whose actor is a process, job, model, or pipeline defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: Human-gated transitions do not scale to hundreds of claims, so the lifecycle will stall at checked.
metadata.verdict_rule: The transition function refuses non-human actors for stages above checked, and the refusal is itself logged.

claims.text: No automated process may advance a claim beyond the checked stage. Transitions to explained, accepted, or digested are effected only by a recorded act of a named human.

alternatives: A single per-anchor record with a longer free-text basis field.
Sub-claims exist but the parent stage is a weighted average of sub-claim stages.
claims.boundary: Anchor readings (the 287-anchor set and successors) and any future headline decipherment claim. Literature claims are governed by C01 but are not required to be bundles.
falsification_tests: An anchor reading displayed or stored as a single-stage, single-score object with no sub-claim records defeats this claim.
A parent stage higher than any one of its sub-claim stages defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: The existing HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/CANDIDATE tier already encodes the bundle's outcome and decomposition is process theatre.
metadata.verdict_rule: Parent stage is computed as the minimum sub-claim stage and is never independently assignable.

claims.text: A decipherment claim (an anchor reading) is a claim bundle of at least four sub-claims — reading soundness, prior-scholarship accounting, attribution, and explanation intelligibility — each with its own evidence record, its own falsifier, and its own stage; the parent claim's stage is the minimum of its sub-claims' stages.

alternatives: Accepted on the strength of a program-internal review note not published for challenge.
Digested inferred from elapsed time since acceptance.
claims.boundary: The accepted and digested transitions for every governed claim.
falsification_tests: A claim at accepted with no explanation record naming a human author defeats this claim.
A claim at digested with no digestion record defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: No external scholar will ever write these accounts, so accepted/digested will be permanently empty and the lifecycle is decorative.
metadata.verdict_rule: The accepted transition validates the explanation record's presence, named authorship, and hash; the digested transition validates the digestion record against the adjudicated threshold.

claims.text: A claim may be marked accepted only when an explanation record exists for it: a readable account artifact (URI plus content hash) authored by a named human, filed where other scholars can challenge it. Digested additionally requires a digestion record evidencing independent scholarly engagement with that account (per the threshold set at adjudication, OD-5).

alternatives: Attribution handled by narrative citation practice (e.g. ATTRIBUTION.md) without a per-claim record.
Contested attribution shown only inside a detail view, not on the parent.
claims.boundary: Decipherment claims (anchor-reading bundles per C03); the cap binds stage, not score or verdict.
falsification_tests: A decipherment claim whose attribution sub-claim is contested while its displayed parent stage exceeds the adjudicated cap defeats this claim.
A decipherment claim with no attribution sub-claim record defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: Completeness of prior scholarship is unprovable, so the sub-claim would be permanently contested and cap everything.
metadata.verdict_rule: Cap enforcement is mechanical: parent stage = min(bundle rule per C03, cap) whenever the attribution contest state is contested.

claims.text: Attribution is a registered sub-claim of every decipherment claim, carrying required evidence: the prior-scholarship search record on which completeness is asserted, the named prior readings accounted for, and a contest state. While attribution is contested, the contest is displayed on the parent claim wherever the parent is displayed, and the parent's stage is capped (default cap: checked, per OD-3).

alternatives: Scores shown with a disclaimer caption while remaining the headline metric.
Counts shown as progress bars toward decipherment.
claims.boundary: Frontend surfaces, API summary responses, generated reports, exports, and public pages produced by the program.
falsification_tests: A surface whose headline or summary position carries a score, band, mean, or count as the claim's standing defeats this claim (the current 'N signs deciphered' headline is a standing counterexample this spec exists to remove).
A verdict display with no not-understood statement defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: Funders and readers need simple summary numbers; removing them hides real progress.
metadata.verdict_rule: Display conformance is checkable per surface: scores appear only inside checking-stage evidence presentations, and the not-understood statement is a required field of every verdict record.

claims.text: No program surface may present an AEE score, score band, mean score, or claim/anchor count as evidence that a claim is accepted or that the script is deciphered; and every verdict display carries an explicit statement of what remains not understood.

alternatives: One combined status with a footnote distinguishing machine from human assessment.
claims.boundary: Claims API responses and every frontend/report rendering of claim standing.
falsification_tests: A rendering in which an AEE band, score, or extraction status occupies the visual position or vocabulary reserved for scholarly acceptance defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: Two displays for one claim will confuse readers more than one honest combined status.
metadata.verdict_rule: API serializes lane1 and lane2 as distinct objects; UI components for the two lanes are distinct and lane-2 components accept no lane-1 fields.

claims.text: Lane-1 state (machine verification: scores, verdicts, extraction and test outcomes) and lane-2 state (human-paced scholarly acceptance: stage at or above explained) are stored as separate fields and rendered in separate display regions with lane-specific labels; no lane-1 value may render in a lane-2 position, label, or colour.

alternatives: Priority handled by publication dates in the literature corpus only.
Registration offered only for readings the program has checked.
claims.boundary: Readings submitted by scholars outside the program. Program-internal predictions remain governed by docs/PREDICTION_REGISTER.md.
falsification_tests: A registration workflow that requires a program verdict, score, or stage before a timestamp is issued defeats this claim.
A registered reading whose credit display changes when the program's assessment of it changes defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: An open register invites speculative land-grabs of low-quality readings.
metadata.verdict_rule: Timestamp issues at intake on completeness of the registration record alone; credit display is a function of the registration record, never of assessment state.

claims.text: An external scholar's reading can be registered in a priority register at intake — claimant, reading, evidence, timestamp — establishing priority and credit independent of the program's stage or verdict on that reading, and the registration itself is never contingent on the program agreeing with the reading.

alternatives: Trails kept in per-phase outcome documents, referenced by phase number only.
claims.boundary: Verdicts and stage transitions recorded after this spec is implemented; historical records are addressed only as OD-1 decides.
falsification_tests: A verdict or stage transition whose claim-level API representation lacks any one of: evidence refs, origin groups, falsifier state, actor, timestamp — defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: Spec-level outcome records already provide trails; per-claim serialization duplicates them.
metadata.verdict_rule: A completeness check over verdict/transition records is part of the claims API's own output contract.

claims.text: Every verdict and every stage transition on a governed claim carries an inspectable evidence trail — evidence references with origin groups, falsifier state, actor (human or named process), and timestamp — retrievable from the claim's own API representation without consulting run logs.

alternatives: The spec PR quietly fixes the DeciphermentPanel headline as an obvious bug.
claims.boundary: Spec 029 and all work done under it before an adjudicated, frozen implementation plan exists.
falsification_tests: A diff under this spec that alters an existing claim record, anchor record, verdict, or display string defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: The headline violation is live now; deferring its fix to a later plan leaves a known misstatement public.
metadata.verdict_rule: The Spec 029 PR diff is confined to specs/029-tao-claim-lifecycle/ and the H1 ledger entry.

claims.text: This spec, as a claims-first draft, itself changes nothing: it re-stages, re-scores, re-words, and re-displays no existing claim, anchor, or verdict. Any application to existing records happens only under a later adjudicated plan and the owner's retroactivity decision (OD-1).

note: Claims-first draft register (2026-10-12). All claims are status draft pending owner adjudication. No plan or tasks exist for this spec; nothing in this register is frozen.
